questions.prompt: Yeast is made of only one cell. Yeast is...
questions.explanation: One cell means unicellular. A tissue is a group of similar cells in a multicellular organism.

questions.prompt: Which kingdom does yeast belong to?
questions.explanation: Yeast is a single-celled fungus. It has a true nucleus, so it is not in Monera.

questions.prompt: Which part of the cell holds the hereditary information?
questions.explanation: The hereditary, or genetic, information is in the nucleus.

questions.prompt: In which organelles does cellular respiration take place?
questions.explanation: Respiration takes place in the mitochondria. Chloroplasts are for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which scientific name is written correctly?
questions.explanation: Capital letter for the genus, small letter for the species.

questions.prompt: Which structure is found only in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells. Mitochondria and the cell membrane are found in both kinds of cell.

questions.prompt: Under a light microscope, onion cells look like neat boxes. Why?
options: Each cell has a rigid cell wall
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall gives plant cells a regular shape. Cheek cells also have a nucleus, and they are not box-shaped.

questions.prompt: Which list is in the correct order from the largest group to the smallest?
questions.explanation: The full order is kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, so class comes before family.

questions.prompt: What does the large central vacuole of a plant cell contain?
questions.explanation: The vacuole holds cell sap: water with dissolved salts and food. Chlorophyll is in the chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: An organism has cells with walls and chlorophyll. Which kingdom does it belong to?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll means it makes its own food by photosynthesis, so it is a plant.
